variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A production Transformer architecture is the complete execution system that turns a trained Transformer checkpoint into a dependable service. It includes the model block, attention and feed-forward kernels, model sharding, KV-cache allocation, request scheduling, batching, streaming, admission control, observability, and recovery.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Validate and admit
pairs.detail: Resolve the model bundle, cap input and output tokens, authenticate the caller, and reserve queue and cache capacity.
pairs.explanation: Resolve the model bundle, cap input and output tokens, authenticate the caller, and reserve queue and cache capacity.

pairs.label: Prefill the prompt
pairs.detail: Run prompt tokens through every block, create the first-token logits, and write reusable key/value state.
pairs.explanation: Run prompt tokens through every block, create the first-token logits, and write reusable key/value state.

pairs.label: Schedule decode
pairs.detail: Continuously combine active sequences, read their cache pages, run one token step, and retire completed work.
pairs.explanation: Continuously combine active sequences, read their cache pages, run one token step, and retire completed work.

pairs.label: Stream and account
pairs.detail: Emit bounded output, record phase-level latency and resource use, release cache pages, and commit terminal status once.
pairs.explanation: Emit bounded output, record phase-level latency and resource use, release cache pages, and commit terminal status once.

pairs.label: Multi-head attention
pairs.detail: Each query head has a corresponding key and value head.
pairs.explanation: Each query head has a corresponding key and value head. It preserves the checkpoint's full projection shape but uses the most KV-cache bytes among these three options.

pairs.label: Grouped-query attention
pairs.detail: Several query heads share each KV head.
pairs.explanation: Several query heads share each KV head. It reduces incremental-decoding cache and bandwidth while retaining more KV groups than MQA.

pairs.label: Multi-query attention
pairs.detail: All query heads share one key head and one value head.
pairs.explanation: All query heads share one key head and one value head. It minimizes KV state for the shape, but the checkpoint must be trained or deliberately converted and evaluated for it.

variants.hint:

Grouped-query attention: Several query heads share each KV head.

Multi-query attention: All query heads share one key head and one value head.

variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Replica parallelism
pairs.detail: Keep a complete model replica on each serving group and route independent requests across replicas.
pairs.explanation: Keep a complete model replica on each serving group and route independent requests across replicas. This gives a simple failure boundary when the model and cache fit.

pairs.label: Tensor parallelism
pairs.detail: Shard matrix operations across tightly connected devices.
pairs.explanation: Shard matrix operations across tightly connected devices. It reduces weight and KV state per device but introduces collectives on the critical token path.

pairs.label: Pipeline parallelism
pairs.detail: Place different layer ranges on different stages.
pairs.explanation: Place different layer ranges on different stages. It helps very deep models fit, but pipeline bubbles, stage imbalance, and failure of any stage affect the whole replica.

pairs.label: Context parallelism
pairs.detail: Partition sequence positions for long-context execution.
pairs.explanation: Partition sequence positions for long-context execution. Attention still needs information across partitions, so the communication pattern must be supported and measured.

Tensor parallelism: Shard matrix operations across tightly connected devices.

Pipeline parallelism: Place different layer ranges on different stages.

pairs.label: Bound the request

pairs.explanation: Estimate prompt and output tokens, deadline, cache pages, priority, and compatible model pool.

pairs.label: Allocate paged state
pairs.detail: Reserve noncontiguous cache blocks so sequence growth does not require one large contiguous allocation.
pairs.explanation: Reserve noncontiguous cache blocks so sequence growth does not require one large contiguous allocation.

pairs.label: Compose an iteration
pairs.detail: Select decode tokens and bounded prefill chunks without exceeding token, sequence, deadline, or memory limits.
pairs.explanation: Select decode tokens and bounded prefill chunks without exceeding token, sequence, deadline, or memory limits.

pairs.label: Retire and refill
pairs.detail: Release completed sequence pages and admit compatible queued work at the next safe iteration boundary.
